answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost.
